records.prompt: Use case: lighting-weather / identity-preserve photographic finishing. Image 1 is the EDIT TARGET. Images 2 and 3 are COLOR/TEXTURE REFERENCES ONLY: the existing Saints of Bad Luck hero and a frame from The Depot Gate. Edit only the photographic finishing of image 1 so it sits quietly alongside those two references. Do not copy any face, object, typography, layout, lighting geometry or scene from images 2/3. Preserve image 1's exact character identity, facial anatomy and expression, gaze, straight-on pose or existing scene pose, wardrobe, background geometry, framing and aspect ratio. This is a restrained color and texture match, NOT a dramatic relight, restaging or redesign. Apply these ten small finishing moves together: (1) modest global exposure reduction, approximately a quarter stop; (2) gently compress the top highlight range so bright white hair, skin and background do not look luminous; (3) give the midtones a little richer density without losing face readability; (4) a soft film toe that keeps dark fabric detail, with no crushed black and no gray fog; (5) tame only excess orange/pink skin chroma while preserving natural color; (6) neutralize brilliant digital whites toward the existing hero's restrained slightly cool/off-white balance; (7) a very subtle muted olive/blue-gray shadow bias related to the references, not a teal/orange LUT; (8) reduce brittle local micro-contrast and oversharpened pore/hair edge halos while retaining genuine texture; (9) fine irregular photographic grain integrated into the tonal structure, visible on close inspection, not dirt, scratches or large noisy speckles; (10) a barely perceptible optical softness in bright transitions, not blur, bloom, glow rings or beauty smoothing. Keep this low-key and modest: no heavy vignette, hard new shadows, sepia wash, dramatic underexposure, plastic skin, changed facial detail, added text, logo, borders or letterboxing. The output must remain image 1, finished to feel like a photographed frame from the same show. Preserve the complete head, shoulders and original margins. Do not bake in a bottom transparency fade; the website already supplies that. For this centered cast portrait, maintain the neutral studio setup and direct gaze. Keep the background plain and subtly darker neutral gray; do not introduce a film location.
